1.why: The system checks that the reset code belongs to the user by validating the sessionId and tokenHash in recovery-verify.

2.why: The system does not allow the same reset code to work for any other user due to session-specific validation.

3.why: Previous sessions are invalidated upon password reset as the session is tied to the recovery process and marked as used.

4.why: The server enforces HTTPS with TLS certificates as seen in Bun.serve configuration.

5.why: Reset codes are hashed with bcrypt and stored securely in recoveryRecords.

6.why: Email messages (simulated logs) do not expose private user data; tokens are only shown in test logs.

7.why: User-supplied data (email, passwords) is sanitized via cleanText and validIdentifier functions.

8.why: Redirect links are controlled by the client-side routing (gatedRoute) and do not allow arbitrary URLs.

9.why: Email templates are not dynamically generated from user input; the system uses static messages.

10.why: Error pages and logs do not expose user private information or tokens (e.g., generic error messages).

11.why: Passwords are hashed with bcrypt and never stored in plaintext; no hardcoded credentials exist.

12.why: The system does not allow default credentials; authentication requires explicit user input.

13.why: The system throttles login attempts (5 failures) and locks the account temporarily (LOCK_TIME_MS).

14.why: The application does not reveal whether a username/email exists (generic message for recovery requests).

15.why: Password reset codes are random (randomToken), complex (32-byte base64url), and user-specific (tied to sessionId).
